content.thinking:
I need to understand the path.

The overdue issue check starts from instrumentation.ts register(), scheduler ticks, or a cron POST route, then queue.ts processes the job. The set of issues is narrowed by filtering archived items, rollup org IDs, closed statuses, and assignee. The job emits events but does not send notifications itself. A `reported` Set prevents the same issue from being announced repeatedly.

I need to trace how a notification reaches one specific person through their chosen channels. I will examine the event registry, notification preferences, and how notification rows become emails or in-app alerts.
I need to examine the overdue issues list, organization rollup IDs, notification preferences, email sending logic after notification insertion, and issue webhook listeners.
I need to understand how notifications are delivered via email versus in-app.

The user frames a background check as happening "while nobody is looking" when the due date passes unnoticed.

I need to trace how alerts actually reach users. I'm checking the digest email job, email service, webhook listeners, and UI bell to see how channels like email, in-app, and webhook are delivered. The user's note about one person receiving the alert through their chosen channels suggests notify() writes a row with resolved channels.

The overdue email template exists, but the overdue job does not send it.

Tracing how alerts reach individual users through their chosen channels. Checking webhook listeners for issue.overdue events, the notification bell UI, and preference resolution. Examining the resolveChannels function to understand channel selection.

resolveChannels returns default channels when no preference exists. It adds in_app if enabled, and email only when allowed and not digest-only. The digestOnly flag suppresses immediate emails but keeps the in-app notification row.

The email channel requires the org's `digest_email` plan flag. When digestOnly is true, email is allowed only if that flag is also enabled. This means digestOnly does not suppress email; it actually preserves it when the flag is active.

I need to trace how the notification reaches the user.

The in-app notification path inserts a row for the UI to read. The webhook service and preference forms are being checked for webhook subscriptions. NotificationChannel includes "webhook" but resolveChannels only pushes "in_app" and "email". Preferences also lack a webhook setting.

The scheduler starts only in Node.js. It registers event handlers and a 60-second tick interval. Each tick checks if overdue-issues jobs are due based on their 60-minute cadence. The first tick always runs because no prior run exists. Jobs are enqueued by minute bucket and drained to execute runOverdueIssueJob.

A POST /api/cron/overdue endpoint can trigger the job directly via cron secret, bypassing the scheduler. The runOverdueIssueJob wrapper enforces a live-only archive guard; if includeArchived is undefined, it returns true and skips the sweep entirely. The repository handles archived issue queries.

The job fetches the oldest 50 measured organizations per pass, ordered by measuredAt ascending. It then queries overdue issues for each organization that are live and past due.

The query filters for backlog, todo, in_progress, and in_review statuses while excluding closed issues. It orders results by dueAt.

For each issue, the job skips null due dates and already-reported IDs. It emits an `issue.overdue` event containing orgId, actorId, occurredAt, issueId, projectId, dueAt, and assigneeId. Successful emissions are added to a process-lifetime Set to prevent duplicates. Failures are logged but not added to that Set so they can retry.

The job itself performs no notification or email logic.

The job ignores assignee notification preferences and does not filter out unassigned issues. It relies on SQL to determine overdue status rather than the UI `isOverdue` helper. The in-memory announcement set is lost on restart, so a later sweep may re-announce an issue that is still open and past due.

The 60-second scheduler tick does not cause the job to run every few minutes; it only checks for due jobs. The cron endpoint can be hit more frequently, but the in-memory reported set still deduplicates within a single process.

If an event bus emit throws, the issue is not added to the reported set, so the next pass retries it.

The notification fan-out subscriber is registered at module load of notification-service. Event-registry imports that service as a side effect when registerEventHandlers runs.

The cron route imports the job runner but not the notification service, so subscribers must be attached separately in tests. Production relies on instrumentation to register handlers first. I still need to check whether webhook listeners subscribe to issue.overdue.

The notification fan-out drops issues with a null assigneeId. For assigned issues, it calls notify with the assignee as recipient and an empty actorId. The notify function loads the organization for plan and flag context. It deduplicates recipients and fetches each recipient's issue_overdue preference to resolve channels.

The overdue email template is located in src/emails/overdue-email.

sendEmail is only invoked by auth-service and digest-email-job. The notification fan-out stores the channel choice on the notification row but does not call sendEmail directly for overdue alerts. Instead, notify() looks up the assignee's issue_overdue preference, and resolveChannels converts their inApp, email, digestOnly, and digest_email flags into the channel list stored on that row.

insertNotifications writes one row per recipient. The inbox reads this row directly. Digest-only recipients receive the overdue alert later through the digest job, which bundles unread notifications into a digest email. Immediate email is recorded on the row but has no separate mailer that sends it right away.

I need to check whether the inbox loads notifications from the database or only from a client store. I will also review the notification preferences form, its update action, the livePredicate archive filter, and the cron secret.

I need to inspect the dashboard notification bell layout and the inbox page to trace how in-app alerts reach specific assignees.

The preferences form should also be checked to see which channels users have selected.

A design gap exists in the notification flow: `notify()` records channels but never calls `sendEmail()`. The digest job later fetches unread notifications for recipients who have the `digest_email` flag, yet it does not filter by whether the stored channel includes "email". This means email drafts may not be generated even when that channel is chosen.

Digest recipients are users with any `digestOnly` preference. If an assignee sets `issue_overdue` to digestOnly, their unread overdue notification is included in the digest email. If they set `email` true but `digestOnly` false, the channel is stored on the row, yet no immediate overdue email is sent. The overdue template in `src/emails/overdue-email.tsx` is a separate test-only system.

The react-email OverdueEmail template is not invoked by the overdue job.

The production overdue path uses notification fan-out instead. The OverdueEmail template is only rendered in tests.
Checking whether OVERDUE_LOOKAHEAD_HOURS is actually used.

I have a solid picture. I will check the user repository for the digest email address path and whether notify skips when the assignee is the only recipient with empty channels.

The scheduler interval starts without an immediate tick, so the first overdue scan waits up to 60 seconds. The cron POST route triggers the job directly instead of through the queue. Both paths share a module-level deduplication set.

The overdue job filters archived issues, batches organizations by oldest measuredAt, and fetches overdue issues while skipping null dueAt values and already-reported IDs. It emits issue.overdue events and tracks reported IDs in a module-level set. Notification, email, and webhook sending are handled by downstream components.

Downstream components must decide recipients, filter by preferences, write activity, persist deduplication across restarts, and handle issue closure or mutation. The event carries only assigneeId, so watchers, authors, and project members are not automatically included. listOverdueIssues also requires dueAt to be strictly past the current time.

Overdue issues are limited to open statuses: backlog, todo, in_progress, and in_review. Unassigned issues are still returned and emitted.

The fan-out step drops null assignees and notifies only the assignee. The actorId is null, so the actor skip does not suppress the assignee. Preferences still apply.

Notifications are persisted via insertNotifications with recipientId and channels JSON.

In-app notifications are fetched by actor.userId for the dashboard bell, inbox page, and notification panel. The user needs permission notification:read on their own notification resource.

The overdue email template is never triggered by this path.

Digest emails are sent by a separate `runDigestEmailJob` on its own cadence. It gathers unread notifications for digest subscribers, renders them with the digest template, and sends to the user's email address. It marks those notifications as read so the same window is not resent.

If an assignee has `digestOnly` preference and the organization has `digest_email`, the email channel remains on the notification row and the assignee is included in `listDigestSubscribers`.

When no preference exists, `resolveChannels` falls back to default channels: `["in_app", "email"]`.

If both in-app and email preferences are disabled, the notification is skipped entirely. When digest-only mode is active, the email channel still appears on the row so the digest job can send it. However, buildDigest ignores the notification's channels array and includes all unread notifications in the digest.

Digest recipients are anyone with any digestOnly preference. An overdue notification can still reach a user who has digestOnly on a different issue type if the immediate email remains unread. If a user mutes email but keeps in-app, they receive only the in-app row and will not receive a digest unless they have digestOnly enabled for another notification type.

The digest job is a coarse opt-in: any digestOnly preference includes the user in the daily bundle of all unread rows. The overdue-specific channel choice is handled by resolveChannels for the issue_overdue kind. notify only inserts a notification row tagged with channels; it does not itself send email.

The overdue check runs in the background while no one is looking. It is not triggered by opening an issue. The UI `isOverdue` flag on cards is purely visual and does not notify anyone.

In `instrumentation.ts`, event handlers are registered before jobs run. This ensures subscribers exist before the scheduler starts. The registration imports the notification service, which triggers its side effects, and then attaches activity, search, usage, webhook, and digest bridges.

The scheduler runs a 60-second `setInterval` that is unref'd and idempotent. Each tick checks due jobs, enqueues them, and drains the queue. The overdue job repeats every 60 minutes. Enqueue IDs use a minute bucket so duplicate ticks in the same minute are ignored. The handler dynamically imports `runOverdueIssueJob` and passes it a fresh `Date`, which may differ slightly from the enqueue timestamp. If the handler throws, the queue retries with backoff up to five attempts.

Per-issue errors inside `runOverdueIssueJob` are caught and logged without throwing. The queue treats the job as successful even when individual emits fail. Failed emits increment a failure counter and remain in the reported set, so the next sweep retries them. Only unexpected exceptions outside the per-issue try block trigger queue retries.

The job adds the issue ID to the `reported` deduplication set immediately after emitting the event, before any catch block. This means a failed notification fan-out still marks the issue as announced and will not be retried on the next sweep.

The job does not confirm delivery. If no subscribers exist, emit returns immediately and the issue is still marked reported. The cron route assumes handlers are already registered in the same process. If notification-service was not imported in that context, the event would be emitted into an empty bus and still marked reported.

The job batches organizations by oldest usage measurement. It queries up to 50 org IDs ordered by measuredAt ascending, skipping any org without a usage row. The usage rollup job updates that timestamp, so the batch rotates each pass and only the oldest organizations are scanned.
Checking whether recomputeUsage updates measuredAt to rotate the org batch.

Checking notificationResource and listNotifications permissions for the inbox actor.

Notification fan-out writes assigneeId as recipient, so only that actor sees the notification. The overdue query hardcodes open statuses explicitly rather than excluding closed ones, which would miss any new status added later.

The overdue check compares ISO-8601 UTC strings lexicographically. An issue due at the exact sweep instant is not overdue yet. The SQL predicate drives the scan, while the UI separately applies `isOverdue` for red styling.

The comment on `resolveChannels` claims `digestOnly` suppresses immediate email, but the code includes email when `digestOnly` is active and a flag is set.

Tests clarify the intended behavior: digestOnly keeps email when the digest flag is on, drops it when off, and bypasses the flag entirely when digestOnly is false. The test represents the true semantics. runDigestEmailJob is a sibling job on the same scheduler.

The digest job emails only users returned by listDigestSubscribers. It pulls unread notifications from a rolling 24-hour window, not from date.ts digestWindow. Each email is logged to the recipient's structured log and then marked as read. The job only runs during the organization's configured digestHourUtc.

The digest job runs roughly once per hour during the organization's configured UTC hour. Its 60-minute cadence is measured from the previous run, not aligned to the hour. If the last digest run occurred within that hour, the next scheduled tick lands in the following hour, so shouldRunForOrg returns false and the job skips.

Digest is the email delivery leg for overdue alerts. The in-app row is the direct product of the fan-out.

Webhooks are not part of the overdue alert path. resolveChannels never adds the webhook channel, and webhook listeners do not subscribe to issue.overdue. Users who chose webhooks are not notified.

Preferences are saved through updateNotificationPreferenceAction, then upserted via preferenceRepo. The fan-out reads them with getPreference. If no row exists, the system falls back to DEFAULT_CHANNELS: in-app and email. The settings page only lists existing preference rows, so an empty form means no saved preferences yet. The explanation will follow the actual execution order.

I will answer the user's explicit question about what the component does not do. I can phrase the boundary as a direct list because the task explicitly asks for it.

An overdue issue is announced by a background sweep, turned into one notification for its assignee, and shown or mailed according to that person's saved channels. Nothing on the issue page starts this.

## What starts the check

On a Node server, `register` in `src/instrumentation.ts` runs once before requests. It calls `registerEventHandlers` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`, then `startScheduler` in `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`. Importing the registry loads `src/server/services/notification-service.ts`, and that module's `registerFanOut` subscribes to `issue.overdue` before the scheduler is armed.

`startScheduler` sets a 60-second interval that calls `tick`. The timer is `unref`'d, and a second `startScheduler` call does nothing. `tick` walks `CADENCE_MINUTES`. `overdue-issues` is due on the first tick and again 60 minutes after `lastRunAt`. When it is due, `tick` calls `enqueue` in `src/server/jobs/queue.ts` with the id `overdue-issues:<minute bucket>`, then `drain`. `enqueue` ignores a duplicate id. `drain` takes due jobs oldest-first and `runHandler` dynamic-imports `runOverdueIssueJob`, passing a fresh `Date`.

The same function can also be started from outside the interval. `POST` in `src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts` calls `assertCronSecret` (header `x-taskflow-cron` must match `TASKFLOW_CRON_SECRET`) and then `runOverdueIssueJob(new Date())` directly. That route does not send mail. It only runs the scan, and the fan-out already attached in this process handles the event.

Opening an issue does not participate. `isOverdue` in `src/lib/date.ts` only paints due dates on cards and the due-date field.

## Which issues count

`runOverdueIssueJob` in `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts` is wrapped by `runJob` from `src/server/jobs/types.ts`. It first calls `shouldFilterArchived` in `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` with an empty scope. An empty scope means "live rows only". If that ever returned false, the sweep logs and returns without scanning.

It then asks `listOrgIdsForRollup` in `src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts` for 50 organization ids, oldest `measuredAt` first. Organizations with no usage row are absent. For each id, `listOverdueIssues` in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` keeps rows that are:

- in that organization (`orgPredicate`)
- live (`livePredicate` adds `archived_at IS NULL`)
- holding a due date (`dueAt` not null)
- already past the sweep timestamp (`dueAt < now`, ISO text compared with `lt`)
- still open: `backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, or `in_review`

`done` and `canceled` are the closed statuses in `CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES` in `src/types/issue.ts`, and they never come back. Results are ordered by `dueAt`. The query does not require an assignee. An unassigned overdue issue is still returned.

Inside the job, a null `dueAt` is skipped again, and any id already in the in-memory `reported` set is skipped. Everything else is announced.

## What the job owns

For each remaining issue it calls `emit` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` with type `issue.overdue`. The payload, typed in `src/types/event.ts`, is the organization, `actorId: null`, the sweep time, the issue id, the project id, `dueAt`, and `assigneeId` (which may be null). On a resolved `emit` it adds the id to `reported` and increments `processed`. A throw increments `failed`, logs, and leaves the id out of `reported`.

`emit` waits for every subscriber with `Promise.allSettled` and does not rethrow a subscriber failure. A fan-out that rejects still counts as announced.

The job does not choose a recipient, read preferences, write a notification row, send mail, write an activity entry, or call a webhook. Activity, search, usage, and webhook listeners in `activity-service.ts`, `search-service.ts`, `usage-service.ts`, and `webhook-service.ts` do not subscribe to `issue.overdue`. The job's own comment states the split: it publishes the fact, and whoever cares reacts on the bus.

## Why the same issue is announced once

`reported` is a module-level `Set<string>` in `overdue-issue-job.ts`. A later sweep still finds the open, past-due issue, sees the id, and does not emit again. `resetOverdueTracking` clears that set for tests only.

The set lasts for the process lifetime. A restarted process starts empty and can announce again. Within one process, the scheduler also waits 60 minutes between `overdue-issues` runs, and a repeated cron call in that process hits the same set. The queue's retry (up to 5 attempts, then drop) only applies when `runHandler` throws. Per-issue failures are caught inside the job, so the queue treats that pass as finished.

## How that one person is told, on the channels they chose

`registerFanOut` handles `issue.overdue` by returning immediately when `assigneeId` is null. Otherwise it calls `notify` with kind `issue_overdue` and a recipient list of exactly that assignee. The title is "An issue is overdue", the body includes the issue id and `dueAt`, the href is `/issues/<issueId>`, and `actorId` is null. Because the actor is null, the "skip the person who caused it" rule in `notify` does not drop the assignee.

`notify` loads the organization, builds a `FlagContext` (plan and flag overrides, role null), and dedupes recipients. For the assignee it calls `getPreference` in `src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts` for `(orgId, userId, "issue_overdue")`. No row means the defaults in `notify`: `in_app` and `email`. A saved row goes through `resolveChannels`:

- `inApp` adds `in_app`.
- `email` adds `email` when the preference is not digest-only, or when it is digest-only and `isEnabled("digest_email", flags)` is true. That flag, in `src/config/feature-flags.ts`, requires the growth plan (or an override).
- An empty channel list writes no row.

`insertNotifications` in `src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts` stores one row whose `recipientId` is the assignee and whose `channels` column is that JSON list.

Those choices are edited on `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/notifications/page.tsx`. The page loads `listPreferences` for the signed-in user and renders `NotificationPreferencesForm`, which has an "Issue overdue" row with in-app, email, and (when `digest_email` is on) digest-only switches. Saving calls `updateNotificationPreferenceAction` in `src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts`, which rejects `digestOnly` when the flag is off, then `updatePreference`, which upserts through `upsertPreference`.

In the app, the row is read back only for that recipient. The dashboard layout calls `listNotifications` with `recipientId: actor.userId` and passes the unread total to `DashboardShell`, then `TopBar`, then `NotificationBell`. The inbox page and the `@panel/notifications` page call `listNotifications` the same way, after `can` allows `notification:read` on `notificationResource` for that user. `listNotifications` in the service checks `assertOrgScope` and `assertCan` before the repository filters `recipient_id`.

Email leaves later, and only for someone who opted into the digest. The same scheduler enqueues `digest-email` on a 60-minute cadence. `runDigestEmailJob` in `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts` walks the same oldest-usage organization batch, keeps organizations whose `settings.digestHourUtc` equals the current UTC hour, and requires `digest_email`. `listDigestRecipients` returns users with any `digestOnly` preference. For each, `buildDigest` in `src/server/services/digest-service.ts` loads unread notifications since 24 hours ago via `listUnreadSince`, including this overdue row. `renderDigest` renders the `digest` template, `findUserById` supplies that user's address, and `sendEmail` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts` records the draft in the log (there is no outbound mail transport). The job then `markRead`s each digested row, so a later run in the same window does not send them again.
